challengeTypes: identify: Which of these is a PHYSICAL change? (Melting of ice vs Burning of wood vs Rusting of iron vs Cooking of food)

sort: Drag each change to physical or chemical (Melting ice = Physical | Burning wood = Chemical | Dissolving salt in water = Physical | Rusting of iron = Chemical | Boiling water = Physical | Cooking food = Chemical | Tearing paper = Physical | Burning paper = Chemical)
identify: Which gas is the most abundant in air? (Nitrogen vs Oxygen vs Carbon dioxide vs Hydrogen)

sort: Drag each gas to its correct percentage in air (Nitrogen = 78% | Oxygen = 21% | Carbon dioxide = 0.04% | Other gases (argon, helium) = about 1% | Nitrogen = most abundant | Oxygen = second most abundant)
identify: During the DAY, which breeze blows and from where? (Sea breeze, from sea to land vs Land breeze, from land to sea | No breeze | Wind from all directions)

sort: Drag each breeze to its correct description (Sea breeze = day time, air flows from sea to land | Land breeze = night time, air flows from land to sea | Sea breeze = because land heats faster than sea during day | Land breeze = because land cools faster than sea at night | Sea breeze = cool air from sea replaces warm air rising from land | Land breeze = cool air from land flows to warmer sea)
identify: What is the purpose of an exhaust fan in a kitchen? (To remove smoke, heat, and odors vs To cool the food vs To provide light vs To decorate the wall)

sort: Drag each ventilation method to its correct purpose (Ventilator near ceiling = lets hot air escape | Exhaust fan in kitchen = removes smoke and odors | Windows = let fresh air in | Air vents = maintain air circulation | Chimney = removes smoke from stove | Exhaust fan in bathroom = removes moisture and odors)
extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) Physical and chemical changes — Physical change: no new substance is formed, usually reversible. Examples: melting ice, boiling water, dissolving salt, tearing paper, cutting wood. Chemical change: a new substance is formed, usually irreversible. Examples: burning wood, rusting iron, cooking food, burning paper, baking a cake. Signs of chemical change: color change, gas produced, heat/light produced, new smell, irreversible. (2) Composition of air — Air is a mixture of gases. Nitrogen 78% (most abundant, does not support burning). Oxygen 21% (supports burning and breathing). Carbon dioxide 0.04% (used by plants for photosynthesis). Other gases like argon, helium about 1%. Water vapor varies. (3) Land and sea breezes — Sea breeze (daytime): land heats up faster than sea, warm air over land rises, cool air from sea flows in to replace it. Breeze flows from sea to land. Land breeze (nighttime): land cools faster than sea, warm air over sea rises, cool air from land flows to sea. Breeze flows from land to sea. (4) Ventilators and exhaust fans — Ventilator: placed near the ceiling, lets hot stale air escape (hot air rises). Exhaust fan: placed in kitchen or bathroom, removes smoke, heat, moisture, and odors by sucking air out. Windows: let fresh air in. Together they maintain air circulation and keep indoor air fresh. Misconceptions: 'all changes are chemical changes' (WRONG — physical changes like melting and dissolving do not form new substances; only chemical changes form new substances), 'air is mostly oxygen' (WRONG — air is 78% nitrogen and only 21% oxygen; nitrogen is the most abundant gas), 'land and sea breezes are the same' (WRONG — sea breeze blows during the day from sea to land; land breeze blows at night from land to sea), 'ventilators are for decoration' (WRONG — ventilators near the ceiling let hot stale air escape since hot air rises), 'exhaust fans bring fresh air in' (WRONG — exhaust fans REMOVE stale air, smoke, and odors; fresh air comes in through windows and vents to replace it).
